newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran seeks 170,000 T sugar for early 1997-traders.
newsitem.headline: Iran seeks 170,000 T sugar for early 1997-traders.

text.p: Iran is looking to buy about 170,000 tonnes of sugar for early-1997 delivery due to reduced local output this year, traders in the Gulf said on Thursday.

"Iran has been tendering in the past five or six weeks to buy 170,000 tonnes of sugar and I think they will get low prices because there are about three trading houses which are long on sugar," a trader said.
"It is likely to be mostly European and Thai sugar delivered in January, February and March (1997)," he added.
"We have reports that production of beet and cane has dropped about 215,000 tonnes this year, perhaps mostly due to weather," a trader said.
Iranian officials were not available for comment.
Iran, a country of about 61 million people, consumes some two million tonnes of sugar a year, about 950,000 tonnes of which are produced domestically, the traders said.
Europe, Thailand, Australia, Cuba, and Brazil are among the main suppliers to Iran.

Tehran has announced plans to achieve sugar self-sufficiency within 10 years. It said in September it was setting up seven sugar cane refining plants with an annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes each and a 100,000-tonne beet refinery.
